workflow: A view-like operation retains access to an owner’s buffer and invokes user-defined hashing or callback logic on that owner.
The callback reentrantly releases the view or clears the owner, deallocating or invalidating the buffer while the outer operation is still active.
The outer operation continues using its previously retained buffer state without rechecking its lifetime.
The access reaches released storage and causes a use-after-free failure instead of returning a recoverable error.
summary: Reentrant callback invalidates backing storage during active operation
decision_reason: The underlying failure is materially the same as a retained pointer or reference being used after its owning buffer is released; the reentrant callback is the mechanism that triggers the owner’s release during the outer operation.
